thread:
jason_support: FYI customer reported parser errors when using structured output (json). Happens intermittently on streaming responses, root cause looks like unescaped line separator + quote mix. Repro below — ccing @emma_dev and @oliver_runtime.

emma_dev: can you paste the exact request they're sending?

jason_support: here's sanitized curl they used:
```\ncurl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"xlarge-001\",\"mode\":\"structured\",\"format\":\"json\",\"prompt\":\"Generate product description in JSON with field 'description'\\nKeep it short\"}'
```

jason_support: Their parser throws SyntaxError in browser: JSON.parse failed at position 124. Logged model response chunk sequence (showing chunk boundaries):
```\nchunk1: {\"id\":\"...\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"{\\\"name\\\":\\\"Widget\\\",\\\"description\\\":\\\"Best-in-class \\\\"}\"}}\nchunk2: {\"delta\":{\"content\":\"performance\\nand reliability\\\",\\\"tags\\\":[\\\"hardware\\\"]}\"}}\n```

emma_dev: Ok this looks like the model emitted an unescaped raw newline inside the JSON string (\n split across chunk boundary) and also used smart quote inside text. That'll break strict parsers.

oliver_runtime: two issues to check: 1) streaming chunk split left a trailing backslash or half-escape, 2) model used U+201C/U+201D smart quotes and U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR which JSON.parse treats as invalid inside string. We need to trace the tokenization & escaping logic in runtime.

lia_sre: tagging infra — any chance proxies are normalizing CRLF? That would convert \n to \r\n and confuse chunking.

jason_support: Customer says it reproduces with a small prompt. They want a quick workaround — suggested client-side sanitize before JSON.parse: replace U+2028/U+2029 with \\u2028/\\u2029, normalize curly quotes to straight ones, and collapse stray CR. Sample JS fix:
```
function safeParse(text){
  const cleaned = text.replace(/\\u2028/g,'\\\\u2028').replace(/\\u2029/g,'\\\\u2029')
                      .replace(/[\\u201C\\u201D]/g,'\"').replace(/\\r\\n/g,'\\n');
  return JSON.parse(cleaned);
}
```

emma_dev: That's a fine workaround, but we should also fix the generator: ensure runtime always encodes JSON strings with escapes for control separators and normalizes quotes in structured mode. I'll add a patch to escape U+2028/2029 and ensure we never emit smart quotes in json mode.

oliver_runtime: I'll also add a streaming sentinel: if a chunk ends with an odd number of backslashes or within a quote, we buffer until quote closes so consumer never sees half-escaped sequences.

support_bot: Incident created: #INC-2024-511 — priority P2. Assigned to emma_dev, oliver_runtime.

jason_support: Customer updated — they can apply client patch but prefer server fix. We'll keep them posted.

emma_dev: I'll open PR with tests (unit + integration) reproducing chunk split and U+2028 case. ETA EOD.

oliver_runtime: noted. Repro case attached to incident.

lia_sre: leaving note: check nginx chunked transfer config and any gzip interactions.

jason_support: thanks all :thumbsup:
